the per-row boot resolution is held by no test: every boot test separates the two boots across two files, so a regression to a per-file boot cache -- the shape the commit message specifically rejects -- would leave the suite green; one file carrying boot A, boot B and a row naming no boot resolves to boots A, B, B at head, so the behaviour exists and only its guard is missing.

The five stated questions, answered with the instrument behind each:

Q1 -- does the pinned-inode test reproduce the collision it claims? Yes. The test file does not exist at the base revision, so it cannot be run there; instead I extracted the head to a scratch tree and reverted the three key declarations (PRIMARY KEY, the ON CONFLICT clause, and UNIQUE) to the base revision's exact text with a driver that refuses unless each block matches exactly once (revert_keys.py), then ran the repo test: both pinned-inode tests fail, test_two_hosts_at_one_inode_and_offset_are_both_kept at assert 2 == 4 on line 723 and test_two_boots_of_one_host_at_one_inode_and_offset_are_both_kept at the same assertion on line 777 (logs/prev-keys-negative-control.txt). _pin_inode(monkeypatch, 424_242) patches Path.stat so every path reports st_ino 424242, which is the shape two node-local records sitting at one path present to a reader. Independently, the ingest report over two files at one path with one pinned inode reads, under the previous keys, rows_inserted 2 with rows_duplicate 2 and node-b absent from the per-host counts, against rows_inserted 4 with 0 duplicates and both hosts at head (logs/prev-keys-report.txt). The claim in the manifest is accurate.

Q2 -- does the node catch throttling.parse_boot_id rather than inheriting its refusal, and is a host-only row distinguishable from a host-and-boot row at every read path? It catches: parse_boot_id is byte-identical between the revisions (the diff of the function is empty and throttling.py is not in the diff), and resolve_boot_id (telemetry_index.py:263) catches its ValueError and returns the unknown-boot sentinel with HOST_SCOPE; key_kind names the key each row got ("host+boot" or "host") and is recorded per row. A host-only row is NOT distinguishable at any read path: the stored columns show it (boot_id '' with key_kind "host" beside a canonical uuid with "host+boot"), but rows() returns the payload's own spelling -- for a row whose boot was "NOT-A-UUID" it reports "NOT-A-UUID" -- and no public surface exposes key_kind, so the conflating paths are rows() (telemetry_index.py:853) and counter_span (telemetry_index.py:812); sum_measurements and time_weighted_mean fold both scopes without exposure too (logs/read-path-scope.txt).

Q3 -- is the boot identity resolved per row rather than per file, and does any per-file cache defeat it? It is, and nothing defeats it. One file carrying a row under boot A, then a row under boot B, then a row naming no boot lands at offsets 0, 139 and 278 under boots A, B and B respectively, all key_kind "host+boot" (logs/per-row-boot.txt); the third row carries the last boot named in its own file, which is what per-row resolution with a carried value means. The only per-file cache is the host (telemetry_index.py:473), deliberate and unchanged in kind. The caveat is durability, not behaviour: no test holds the property (FINDING at tests/test_telemetry_index.py:736).

Q4 -- did discover and ingest stay stable for the concurrent watcher? Yes, by comparison of the two revisions: "def discover(directory: str | Path, pattern: str | None = None) -> list[Path]" and "def ingest(self, sources: Iterable[str | Path]) -> IngestReport" are textually identical between ecd1869b (lines 213, 271) and 273853b5 (lines 350, 426). The consumer on main, landed after this head, calls discover(directory) at watch.py:688 and :731 and index.ingest(sources) at watch.py:690 and :733, all matching. telemetry_store.compact_file gained host and boot_id as keyword-only parameters with defaults, so the receipt recorder's existing calls (serving_receipts.py:381 and :577) still bind.

Q5 -- are the two recorded follow-ons genuine out-of-scope items or in-scope gaps? Follow-on one, "no query surface filters by host so every reader sees every host", is genuine as a filtering concern, but it understates its own scope: counter_span does not merely include every host, it differences across hosts and can return a forward figure no machine advanced (1050.0 measured, logs/span-mixing.txt), and this change is what makes the second host's rows reachable at one path while partitioning time_weighted_mean in the same commit -- that half is an in-scope gap, carried as a finding. Follow-on two, "nothing validates a misreported nodename", is genuine: no host registry exists anywhere in the tree to validate against, so closing it means building a new authority, not repairing this change. Follow-on three, "rebuild() not automatic", is genuine: it is an operational concern for an existing index file. No triage or fix of any finding belongs to this node's scope.
